label: Apollo
description: Arcade tools designed for LLMs to interact with Apollo.io sales intelligence

tools.name: EnrichOrganization
tools.description:
Turn a company domain into firmographics (industry, size, revenue, funding,
location) so a rep can qualify and size an account. Consumes one enrichment
credit on a match; when the plan is out of credits the result reports
status=insufficient_credits rather than failing.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Company domain to look up, such as apollo.io. A full URL or www prefix is accepted and normalized.

output.description: The matched company, or found=False when no match.

tools.name: EnrichPerson
tools.description:
Turn a known person into a verified profile with their current role and,
on request, contact details. Provide at least one identifier: an Apollo person
ID, a name (or first and last name), an email, or a LinkedIn URL; an employer
name or domain alone is not enough to identify someone. Consumes one enrichment
credit on a match; when the plan is out of credits the result reports
status=insufficient_credits rather than failing.

parameters.name: person_id
parameters.description: Apollo person ID, such as the id from a people search result. The most reliable identifier when available. Defaults to matching on the other identifiers.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Full name of the person. Defaults to matching on the other identifiers.

parameters.name: first_name
parameters.description: First name, paired with last_name. Defaults to matching on the other identifiers.

parameters.name: last_name
parameters.description: Last name, paired with first_name. Defaults to matching on the other identifiers.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Known email address of the person. Defaults to matching on the other identifiers.

parameters.name: organization_name
parameters.description: Employer name to disambiguate a name match. Defaults to no employer name.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Employer domain to disambiguate a name match. Defaults to no employer domain.

parameters.name: linkedin_url
parameters.description: LinkedIn profile URL of the person. Defaults to matching on the other identifiers.

parameters.name: reveal_work_email
parameters.description: When True, include the matched person's work email in the result. A successful match consumes an enrichment credit whether or not this is set, so the flag controls only whether the email value is surfaced. Defaults to False.

output.description: The matched person, or found=False when no match.

tools.name: GetApiUsage
tools.description:
Report per-endpoint rate limits and how many requests remain, so the agent
can pace a batch of lookups and avoid being throttled. Requires an Apollo
master API key.

output.description: Per-endpoint rate limits and remaining request counts.

tools.name: SearchOrganizations
tools.description:
Find companies in Apollo's database that match a firmographic profile so a
rep can prioritize the accounts worth working. Results include firmographics
inline unless include_firmographics is disabled. Company search consumes plan
credits; when the plan is out of credits the result reports
status=insufficient_credits with an empty list rather than failing.

parameters.name: keyword_tags
parameters.description: Industry or keyword tags to match, such as fintech or cybersecurity. Defaults to any tags.

parameters.name: locations
parameters.description: Only include companies headquartered in any of these locations, such as a city, state, or country. Defaults to any location.

parameters.name: num_employees_ranges
parameters.description: Only include companies whose headcount falls in any of these ranges, each formatted as min,max (for example 51,200). Defaults to any headcount.

parameters.name: revenue_min
parameters.description: Minimum annual revenue in whole dollars. Defaults to no minimum.

parameters.name: revenue_max
parameters.description: Maximum annual revenue in whole dollars. Defaults to no maximum.

parameters.name: technology_uids
parameters.description: Apollo technology UIDs the company must use. Defaults to any technology.

parameters.name: include_firmographics
parameters.description: When True, backfill each result with firmographics (industry, headcount, location, revenue, founded year) via enrichment so accounts can be ranked without a separate lookup; set False for a faster, lighter name/domain-only list. Defaults to True.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum companies to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position into the matches. Defaults to 0 (first result).

tools.name: SearchPeople
tools.description:
Find people in Apollo's database by role and the firmographics of their
employer. Returns lightweight records without email or phone; use person
enrichment to reveal verified contact details.

parameters.name: person_titles
parameters.description: Job titles to match, such as VP of Sales. Matched loosely unless include_similar_titles is disabled. Defaults to any title.

parameters.name: person_seniorities
parameters.description: Only include people whose current role is at any of these seniority levels. Defaults to any seniority.

parameters.name: person_locations
parameters.description: Only include people located in any of these locations, such as a city, state, or country. Defaults to any location.

parameters.name: organization_locations
parameters.description: Only include people whose employer is headquartered in any of these locations. Defaults to any location.

parameters.name: organization_num_employees_ranges
parameters.description: Only include people whose employer's headcount falls in any of these ranges, each formatted as min,max (for example 51,200). Defaults to any headcount.

parameters.name: employer_domains
parameters.description: Company domains the person must work at. Defaults to any company.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description: Free-text keywords matched across the person's profile. Defaults to no keywords.

parameters.name: include_similar_titles
parameters.description: When True, titles match loosely (similar titles included). Set False to keep only people whose title exactly matches one of person_titles. Defaults to True.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum people to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position into the matches. Defaults to 0 (first result).

summary:
## Apollo Toolkit

Arcade toolkit for interacting with [Apollo.io](https://apollo.io), enabling LLMs to search Apollo's sales intelligence database and enrich company and contact records.

## Capabilities

- **Company intelligence:** Search Apollo's database by firmographic filters (industry, size, revenue, location) to surface and prioritize target accounts; enrich a domain into a full firmographic profile including funding and headcount.
- **People intelligence:** Search contacts by role and employer firmographics; enrich known individuals (by Apollo ID, name, email, or LinkedIn URL) into verified profiles with current role and optional contact details.
- **Credit-aware responses:** Enrichment and search operations consume plan credits; when credits are exhausted, tools return a structured `status=insufficient_credits` result rather than raising an error, letting the agent handle the condition gracefully.
- **Rate-limit visibility:** Retrieve per-endpoint rate-limit status and remaining request counts so agents can pace batch operations and avoid throttling.

## Secrets

`APOLLO_API_KEY` — A REST API key issued by Apollo.io, used to authenticate every request to the Apollo API. Obtain it from your Apollo account under **Settings → Integrations → API Keys** (requires an Apollo account on any paid plan; some endpoints such as `GetApiUsage` specifically require a *master* API key rather than a restricted key). Apollo's API key documentation is available at [https://apolloio.github.io/apollo-api-docs/](https://apolloio.github.io/apollo-api-docs/).

See the [Arcade secrets guide](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets) for how to configure secrets, or manage them directly at [https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets](https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets).
